newsitem.title: FRANCE: Havas Adv to make 300 mln net in 1999 - boss.
newsitem.headline: Havas Adv to make 300 mln net in 1999 - boss.

text.p: Havas Advertising, a unit of Havas, should have net attributable profit of 300 million francs in 1999, its chairman, Alain de Pouzilhac, said in an interview published on Friday.
He told advertising industry weekly Strategies that Havas Advertising would have gross income of over five billion francs in 1999 and was on target to have repaid borrowings by then.

"We are well on the way to achieving our programme of repaying borrowings in 1999 at the latest. At that point gross income will be over five billion francs and our net attributable profit 300 million francs," de Pouzilhac said.

In 1996 Havas Advertising reported net attributable profit of 190.8 million francs after exceptionals and 192.2 million before exceptionals, on gross income of four billion francs. Net debt was 896 million francs.
De Pouzilhac said Havas Advertising faced most problems in Europe. It was still losing money in Germany, where a new boss, Gerhard Schoeps, took over on March 1.
In France the company was only showing one percent growth at constant structure, but its agencies have set their objective for 1997 at growth of four to five percent, he said.
However, in North America, which represents 25 percent of Havas Advertising's gross income, growth was 20 percent, while in Asia-Pacific the company was experiencing 24 percent growth.
Latin America, where it has only just opened for business, already represents two percent of gross income, he added.
